profilePeriod: Political career through September 2026; prime minister 2013–2015, with later published positions explicitly included.
scopeNote: Answers are editorial simulations of documented political principles, not a questionnaire completed by the person. Brazil-specific statements are interpreted in the analogous home-country context. Modern hypothetical technologies require inference.

sources.title: Abbott signals greater sovereignty for states
sources.evidence: Released federation white-paper terms; proposed each level becoming sovereign within its sphere to reduce duplication.

sources.title: Fixing the federation: a tale of two Tonys
sources.evidence: Contrasts 2009 Battlelines proposal to expand Commonwealth legal authority with 2014 decentralizing reform language.

sources.title: Address to Samuel Griffith Society
sources.evidence: Still advocates separate sovereign spheres; defends welfare eligibility restraint, GP co-payment, budget repair and trade agreements; opposes expansive racial speech prosecutions.

sources.title: Abbott hopes Australian republic never happens
sources.evidence: Defends constitutional monarchy as an evolved democratic system with a Crown above party politics.

sources.title: My Address to CPAC
sources.evidence: Advocates nuclear energy, industry and lower taxes; praises carbon-tax repeal and trade agreements; supports party members choosing candidates and debating policy; argues immigration must fall and newcomers assimilate. Rejects net zero while supporting limited-cost conservation. Continues opposition to same-sex marriage.

sources.title: Australia Must Rethink Immigration
sources.evidence: Describes indissoluble federal Commonwealth under Crown, indigenous heritage, British foundation and immigrant character; calls for tighter migration control. Available opening text only.

sources.title: Family First, Migration Second
sources.evidence: Calls for much lower immigration, tougher citizenship tests and longer probation; prioritizes childbearing and family tax/leave support. Acknowledges unconventional families can be loving and migration can benefit a nation; criticizes self-declared gender and multicultural fragmentation.

sources.title: Joint press conference on data retention
sources.evidence: Personally advocates mandatory metadata retention for counterterrorism, child-abuse and other crime investigations; legislation considered by parliamentary intelligence committee.

sources.title: Free speech under siege, Australia’s Future S5E14
sources.evidence: Episode description, recorded September 3, identifies Abbott opposing Digital Duty of Care and section 18C restrictions on speech. Audio not independently transcribed.

sources.title: Abbott on gun control
sources.evidence: ABC interview description directly records Abbott opposing importation of rapid-fire weapons.

sources.title: Bali Nine mercy
sources.evidence: Opposed capital punishment domestically and abroad.

sources.title: Abbott criticizes pandemic response
sources.evidence: Criticized pandemic restrictions as disproportionate.

sources.title: No jab no play and no pay interview
sources.evidence: Supported vaccination-conditioned childcare benefits and childcare safety.

sources.title: Taiwan Matters Too
sources.evidence: Supports deterrence through Australian deployments in Japan, assisting Taiwanese defences, reducing Chinese intermediate goods in strategic supply chains; separates criticism of Beijing from Chinese Australians.

sources.title: Political Managerialism Weakens Australia
sources.evidence: Approves US-Israeli preemptive action against Iranian regime, faults Australian reluctance to assist US; advocates immediate defence capacity including drones and allied Taiwan contingency planning.

sources.title: Promise check: sale of Medibank Private
sources.evidence: Checks successful sale of all Commonwealth Medibank Private shares in November 2014, distinguishing insurer from Medicare.

sources.title: The Ailing of the West
sources.evidence: Says freer trade enriches the world, yet acknowledges China’s relative strategic gains. Defends welfare restraint, industrial energy and American-led defeat of Islamic State.

sources.title: NSW abortion changes
sources.evidence: Abbott spoke at anti-abortion rally opposing mandated referrals as infringement of freedom of conscience.

sources.title: Abbott remains unconvinced of stem cell benefits
sources.evidence: Opposed therapeutic cloning and creating potential human life for research; this limits extrapolation from industrial enthusiasm to biotechnology.

sources.title: Battlelines official publisher listing
sources.evidence: Identifies Tony Abbott as author and describes Liberal Party policy manifesto plus political development; this is political writing, not a personal-only memoir.

sources.title: Battlelines library catalogue
sources.evidence: Catalogue verifies author Tony Abbott, English title, Melbourne University Publishing and 2009 publication.

facts: 2014 and 2016 support autonomy of each governmental tier.
2009 advocated stronger Commonwealth authority; 2026 retains indissoluble federation.
estrutura.tension: Administrative federalism does not imply secession, cultural legal enclaves or abolition of national standards.

facts: Defends parliamentary constitutional monarchy.
2025 asks party members to debate policy and choose candidates; recognizes voters must renew party legitimacy.
representacao.tension: Hereditary symbolic head of state is not endorsement of unelected executive government; dislikes excessive party faction control.

facts: Supported metadata retention, restrictive guns and vaccine benefit conditions.
Opposed death penalty; 2024 criticized pandemic restrictions; 2026 opposed digital speech regulation.
poder.tension: National-security coercion coexists with free speech and later opposition to sweeping health restrictions; no support for universal arbitrary detention inferred.

facts: 2026 wants lower migration, tougher citizenship tests, assimilation and family formation.
Acknowledges migrant nation and benefits of suitable newcomers.
imigracao.tension: Selective immigration and cultural assimilation, not blanket exclusion of every migrant or private ancestral practice.

facts: 2023 proposes active Taiwan deterrence and Australian deployments in Japan.
2026 advocates modern defence capabilities and approves preemptive action against Iran.
diplomacia.tension: Alliance-based military readiness does not mean compulsory conscription, nuclear proliferation or automatic war over every dispute.

facts: Advocates assisting US wars and allied defence of Taiwan.
Approves pressure on Iranian regime and external deployments.
intervencao.tension: Assertive allied intervention differs from territorial annexation or rejection of all international agreements.

facts: Privatized Medibank Private.
Defended welfare restraint and GP co-payment; still advocates family tax and parental-leave support.
economia.tension: Private enterprise preference does not mean privatizing police, abolishing Medicare or rejecting every redistributive safety net.

facts: Advocates smaller government, lower taxes and deregulation.
Supported public infrastructure; favors selective family supports.
controle.tension: Not anarcho-capitalist; conventional monetary institutions and safety net remain; no detailed cryptocurrency position verified.

facts: Praises free-trade agreements and global gains from trade.
Advocates removing Chinese goods from strategic supply chains.
comercio.tension: General free trade with security exceptions, not indiscriminate tariffs and not borderless strategic dependence.

facts: Defends Judaeo-Christian ethos, religious conscience, family and inherited institutions.
religiao.tension: Religious public morality within constitutional democracy; no verified proposal for clerical rule or civil disenfranchisement of unbelievers.

facts: Continues objections to same-sex marriage and gender self-identification.
Opposes abortion referral compulsion; supports natality and traditional family.
moral.tension: Explicitly recognizes loving unconventional families; traditionalism does not require criminalizing all affection or excluding women from careers.

facts: Advocates nuclear power and productive industry over rapid emissions cuts.
Opposed therapeutic cloning and instrumental use of embryos.
tecnologia.tension: Industrial modernity plus moral limits on human enhancement; chips, cultured meat and specific AI deployment remain inferred, not direct quotations.

uncertainties: Checked public material through 2026-10-01; latest directly relevant item accessed is September 2026 speech-policy episode description. Absence of later position is not proven.
Brazil-specific questions are analogical applications to Australian institutions, not invented claims about Brazil.
Unspecified technology, cryptocurrency, municipal schooling and jury-selection policy answers are reasoned extrapolations with moderate strength, never claimed direct positions.
2006 embryo opposition is dated, with no verified later reversal. 2009 centralizing federation argument is weighed against explicit 2014/2016 decentralizing reform.
Some PM transcript follow-up retrievals timed out; no claims depend on unavailable portions.
Three independent reporting/catalogue institutions consulted: ABC, SBS/AAP and WorldCat, alongside primary speeches, government transcripts and publisher.

bookDecision.reason: Battlelines is Abbott’s own substantial policy manifesto and political memoir, first published 2009; chosen over narrower constitutional works. No existing books.json item. Portuguese/Brazilian edition searches yielded no verified translation, so retain original title. No book file modified.
